licence_scope.whole_PDF_redistribution: Article-level CC BY 4.0 grants reproduction/sharing in whole or part. Complete source article copies include their licence, original author/copyright/artist acknowledgements and all source materials. Full-text, caption, figure artwork and rights-page review found no separate excluded copyright credit in these two PDFs. Approval applies to unchanged contextual source article copying with attribution/licence/change notice, not standalone reuse of institutional/publisher marks or any externally referenced source work.
licence_scope.2018_artist_exception_analysis: Acknowledgement says illustrations created for this publication; Figs1-2 printed artist credit and Figs1-3 UR Medicine insignia remain intact. This is affirmative creation/provenance credit, not an exclusion or reprint permission block. No separate excluded-licence line was found; retain exact credits.
licence_scope.2025_third_party_exception_analysis: Primary licence explicitly includes images/third-party material unless otherwise stated by a credit line. Full figure/caption and both pages show no exclusion line.
licence_scope.other_rights: CC BY does not establish privacy/publicity/clinical consent or trademark permissions. Source case diagnoses, patient identity and clinical testing/publication consent remain author reports; this review grants no clinical approval.

issues.finding: Primary 2018 PDF p15/XML/publisher acknowledgement says Nadezhda Kiriyak. Printed artwork credit on Figs 1 and 2 says Nadezhda D. Kiriyak. Proposed external attributions and owner proof use Kiryak.
issues.needed: Preserve published acknowledgement spelling Kiriyak and artwork printed name Nadezhda D. Kiriyak, plus Margaret Kowaluk and University of Rochester credits. Do not change source artwork.

issues.finding: Figure 18c visibly contains LEFT T-7, while row-level laterality is not_reported and the marker is not represented separately. Caption does not specify the side/level.
issues.needed: Record this as the source-burned acquisition-panel marker only; do not infer intramedullary lesion side, the entire vascular course, or independently establish feeder location from this marker.

issues.finding: C6-T10 is correct source-reported extent from the article abstract/case presentation, but not from the figure caption; anatomical_sites_from_source_caption currently attributes it to the caption.
issues.needed: Label the article-case text basis explicitly; keep actual caption unchanged and central gray matter H-pattern caption provenance distinct.

issues.finding: Source RGB ICC samples/profile are identical, but MOGAD PDF image object /Intent is /RelativeColorimetric while retained ICC header rendering intent is 0/perceptual. PDF OutputIntent sRGB profiles are retained in unchanged PDF.
issues.needed: Record source PDF object rendering intent and qualify standalone browser/display colour equivalence as unverified. This does not change pixel/profile bytes or reject the source grant.

issues.finding: Field/curriculum parity is complete, but the claim every named source/guide condition is instantiated exceeds the draft: 2018 Fig2 names Herpes/Polio/Post-vaccination, Fig1 names spinothalamic/lateral corticospinal tracts, and the guide TM table explicitly names infectious/postvaccinal/systemic/paraneoplastic/exposure contexts represented only by broad buckets. The guide differential graphic also names lymphoma, Herpes/VZV, HIV/VM/TB, Toxo/Fungus and cysticercosis.
issues.needed: Retain exact named pending source requirements/context crosswalk or narrow the complete-source enumeration claim. Counts are scaffold obligations, not verified fine anatomy.

byte_preservation.MOGAD_whitespace_span: An intersecting whitespace-only PDF text span was found by span-bounds testing; it contributes no visible glyph or annotation and does not contradict zero meaningful overlay.

figures.source_caption: Intramedullary spinal cord anatomy
Differentiating intramedullary pathology: location within the cord
Differentiating intramedullary pathology: short segment (left) versus long segment (right) lesions

Multiple sclerosis. A 50-year-old male with a history of multiple sclerosis.  a  Axial MERGE image demonstrates partial cord involvement—focal hyperintensity within the right lateral cord with a characteristic triangular shape (arrow). There is no cord enlargement.  b  Sagittal T2 fat-saturated image demonstrates several scattered, short-segment foci of T2 hyperintensity (brackets)

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: spinal cord; regional level not reported in caption

figures.source_caption: Multiple sclerosis. A 50-year-old female with prior history of visual changes, presenting with right extremity weakness.  a  Sagittal STIR image shows several foci of short segment hyperintensity (brackets).  b  Axial T2 image demonstrates partial cord involvement, with a triangular lesion involving the right lateral cord (arrow).  c  Axial T1 post-contrast image demonstrates associated enhancement (arrow), consistent with active demyelination

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: spinal cord; regional level not reported in caption

figures.source_caption: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disease. A 20-year-old female presents with lower back pain and difficulty walking.  a  Sagittal T2 fat-saturated image demonstrates multiple areas of long-segment hyperintensity (arrows).  b  Axial T1 post-contrast image of the orbits reveals subtle right optic nerve enhancement (arrow).  c  Axial T2 image shows central cord involvement (arrow).  d  Axial T1 post-contrast image demonstrates corresponding enhancement (arrow)

source_case_context.laterality: right optic nerve; cord side not reported

figures.source_caption: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM). A 2-year-old boy with recent upper respiratory tract infection and low-grade fevers presents with lower extremity weakness and difficulty walking.  a  and  b  Sagittal T2 images of the cervical and thoracic spine demonstrate long-segment areas of hyperintensity involving the cervical and thoracic spinal cord (arrows). There is mild associated cord swelling.  c  Axial T2 FLAIR image shows mass-like hyperintensity within the thalami (arrow).  d  Follow-up sagittal T2 image of the thoracic spine demonstrates resolution of the previously seen lesions—normal cord

Guillian-Barré syndrome. A 2-year-old patient status post-viral prodrome with progressive ascending weakness/paralysis.  a  Sagittal T2 image of the thoracolumbar spine demonstrates subtle hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris (arrow).  b  Axial T1 post-contrast image of the lumbar spine demonstrates enhancement of multiple nerve roots (arrows)

Transverse myelitis. A 38-year-old female with progressive bilateral extremity and back numbness.  a  Sagittal T2 image demonstrates short segment hyperintensity (bracket) with slight expansion of the cervical cord  b  Axial T2 image demonstrates greater than 2/3 cord involvement (arrow). c T1 post-contrast image demonstrates corresponding dusky enhancement

source_panel_sequences.c: T1 post-contrast; plane not explicitly named

figures.source_caption: HIV myelitis. A 54-year-old female with a history of HIV presents with peripheral neuropathy.  a  Sagittal T2-weighted image demonstrates a long segment of hyperintensity in the dorsal cord.  b  Axial T2-weighted image shows a well-defined dorsal cord lesion (arrowhead) with normal signal within the remainder of the cord.  c  Sagittal T1 post- contrast image shows no enhancement

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: dorsal spinal cord; regional level not reported in caption

figures.source_caption: Subacute combined degeneration due to copper deficiency. A 45-year-old female with tingling in the bilateral upper and lower extremities.  a  Axial T2 image shows hyperintensity in the dorsal columns in an ‘inverted-V’ configuration (arrow).  b  Sagittal T2 image demonstrates long-segment T2 hyperintensity within the dorsal cord (bracket)

source_case_context.source_reported_condition: subacute combined degeneration due to copper deficiency

figures.source_caption: Subacute combined degeneration due to vitamin B12 deficiency secondary to pernicious anemia. A 58-year-old female with tingling in her hands and feet.  a  Pre-treatment sagittal T2 image demonstrates a long segment of high signal in the dorsal cord (bracket).  b  Post-treatment sagittal T2 image demonstrates resolution of the cord signal abnormality

source_case_context.source_reported_condition: subacute combined degeneration due to vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anaemia

figures.source_caption: Ependymoma. A 38-year-old female with pulse-like sensation in both hands.  a  and  b  T2 hyperintense mass (arrow) involves more than two vertebral body levels within the central cord.  c  Minimal heterogeneous enhancement (arrow) on the T1 post-contrast image

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: central spinal cord; more than two vertebral body levels

source_panel_sequences.c: T1 post-contrast; plane not explicitly named

figures.source_caption: Hemangioblastoma. A 40-year-old male with neck spasms and gait disturbance.  a  and  b  Spinal cord syrinx involving the entirety of the cervical cord extends superiorly to the cervicomedullary junction, where there is mass effect on the brainstem with resulting edema (arrow); therefore, more inferior spine imaging was obtained to look for the cause.  c  Sagittal T2 image shows an intramedullary lesion within the lower thoracic cord with associated syrinx (arrow). Serpiginous flow voids (arrowhead) are feeding vessels.  d  T1 post-contrast fat-saturated image demonstrates a nodule of homogeneous enhancement

source_panel_sequences.a: cervical syrinx/brainstem image; sequence not explicitly named
source_panel_sequences.b: cervicomedullary/brainstem image; sequence not explicitly named

figures.source_caption: Spinal astrocytoma. A 3 year old with a history of torticollis and ear pain.  a  Sagittal T2 image demonstrates a heterogeneous, expansile solid and cystic mass involving the upper cervical spine and brainstem, compressing the fourth ventricle and cerebellum (arrow). Mass/edema extends inferiorly to the C7-T1 vertebral level (arrowhead).  b  There is heterogeneous enhancement of the solid components on the T1 post-contrast image (arrow)

source_panel_sequences.b: T1 post-contrast; plane not explicitly named

figures.source_caption: Spinal Cord Metastasis. A 69-year-old male with a history of small cell lung cancer and new back pain.  a  There is a focus of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity (arrow), which enhances ( b , arrow) on the T1 post-contrast coronal image

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: intramedullary spinal cord; regional level not reported in caption

figures.source_caption: Glioblastoma multiforme. A 46-year-old female with lumbar back pain and recent onset of urinary retention. There is an expansile lesion within the distal spinal cord with intermediate T2 hyperintensity ( a , arrow) and non-uniform enhancement ( c , arrowhead)

source_panel_sequences.b: caption does not explicitly identify sequence
source_panel_sequences.c: post-contrast image; exact sequence/plane not explicitly named

figures.source_caption: Dural arteriovenous fistula. A 50-year-old male with gradual onset of inability to walk, off and on constipation, and urinary incontinence.  a  Axial T2 image demonstrates hyperintensity in the cord and multiple serpiginous flow voids (arrow) within the thecal sac.  b  Sagittal T2 image reveals long segment involvement (bracket).  c  Conventional spinal angiogram shows injection of a paraspinal artery with simultaneous robust filling of a corkscrew venous vessel

c.basis: preserved source angiogram artwork; not reported in caption

figures.source_caption: Dural arteriovenous fistula. A 72-year-old male with progressive lower extremity weakness, without improvement in symptoms after lumbar laminectomy.  a  Axial T2 image demonstrates numerous flow voids in the thecal sac (arrowhead). There is high signal in the cord due to congestion (arrow).  b  There is long-segment high T2 signal in the cord, with serpiginous vessels in the posterior thecal sac (bracket).  c  Spinal angiogram shows the right T4–T5 supreme intercostal artery as a feeding vessel.  d  MRA confirms the arteriovenous connection

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: right T4-T5 supreme intercostal feeding artery
source_case_context.laterality: right feeding artery; cord side not reported

figures.source_caption: Arteriovenous malformation. A 16-year-old male with left leg weakness and progressive areflexia.  a  Sagittal T2 fat-saturated image demonstrates a conglomeration of flow voids within the cord parenchyma with surrounding hyperintensity. Prominent extramedullary flow voids lead to this conglomeration of vessels (arrow).  b  The sagittal T1 post-contrast image shows a nodule of enhancement (arrowhead).  c  Conventional angiogram shows an artery feeding a nidus (arrow), which is drained by a prominent vein

source_case_context.laterality: clinical left leg symptoms; lesion side not reported

figures.source_caption: Cavernoma. A 40-year-old female with left upper extremity numbness.  a  Sagittal T2 image shows a short segment mixed signal lesion and layering of low signal at the inferior aspect.  b  The lesion is hypointense on the sagittal GRE image.  c  Sagittal T1 post-contrast image shows minimal strands of enhancement

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: spinal cord; regional level not reported in caption
source_case_context.laterality: clinical left upper limb symptoms; lesion side not reported

figures.source_caption: Spinal cord infarction. An 82-year-old female with hypertension and hyperlipidaemia presents with acute bilateral lower extremity weakness.  a  Axial T2 image demonstrates a large cross-sectional area of hyperintensity (arrow) within the thoracic cord.  b  Axial CT angiogram image shows mural thrombus within the aorta (arrow) at the same level of the spinal cord findings with no appreciable filling of the lumbar arteries. Sagittal T2 ( c ), DWI ( d ) and ADC ( e ) images reveal a long-segment intramedullary lesion in the lower cord (arrows) that is T2 hyperintense and has restricted diffusion

anatomical_sites_from_source_caption: aorta and lumbar artery filling context
source_case_context.laterality: bilateral symptoms; lesion side not reported

figures.source_caption: Compressive myelopathy. A 50-year-old patient with bilateral hand tingling.  a  Sagittal T2 image shows severe spinal canal narrowing at C3–C4 due to degenerative changes, with focal faint signal hyperintensity (arrow).  b  Post-contrast image shows focal enhancement (arrow)

figures.source_caption: Hirayama disease. A 22-year-old male with upper extremity weakness and muscle atrophy.  a  There is focal T2 hyperintensity in the anterior horns (arrowheads). Subtle asymmetric focal cord atrophy at this level (C5–C6), slightly more conspicuous on the left (arrow).  b  Flexion view shows anterior displacement of the dura (arrows) with narrowing of the thecal sac (bracket), extending from C3 to T2, most pronounced at C5–C6. Note the long segment T2 hyperintensity within the anterior horns
